answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard computational proof-of-work per identity to act as the zenith for network security. The verifier acts as a digital harvester, checking that each hash output is a fresh, non-reusable fable of energy expenditure. While an honest agent pays this base cost for one entry, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles to siphon the network nectar, hitting a wall of processing debt. This mechanism assumes compute cannot be pooled; fraud triggers a permanent burn of the identity's state and invalidates all pending claims.
